sections.h2: Where is Conway, Arkansas, and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Conway is the county seat of Faulkner County, in Central Arkansas, about 30 miles northwest of Little Rock. The city sits at 331 feet of elevation and covers roughly 46 square miles, nearly all of it land.

The town began in 1872 as "Conway Station," laid out by Asa P. Robinson, chief engineer of the Little Rock and Fort Smith Railroad. It was incorporated on October 16, 1875. The railroad still shapes the older core, although Conway has no passenger rail service today.

Interstate 40 wraps the northern and eastern edges of the city, with Conway exits numbered 124 through 132. US 64 and US 65 cross town as well. Little Rock is 30 miles away and Russellville 46, so many Conway houses are a short drive from an interstate ramp.

Lake Conway, on the city's edge, is described as the largest man-made lake built by a state game and fish commission in the country. Homes near the water draw a different crowd of buyers than homes near the campuses downtown.

The population grew 8.9% between 2010 and 2020, from 58,908 to 64,134. A young median age fits a college town, and it also tells you that a large part of local demand comes from first-time buyers and renters.

Conway's largest employers are health care, higher education, data services and the school district. A May 2023 list of the biggest employers shows how mixed the base is:

  • Conway Regional Health System: 1,650 employees
  • University of Central Arkansas: 1,600
  • Acxiom: 1,450
  • Conway Public School District: 1,150
  • Conway Human Development Center: 900
  • Walmart: 825
  • Gainwell Technologies and Virco Manufacturing: 650 each
  • Home BancShares and Nabholz Construction: 550 each

The city has also seen plants come and go. The IC Corporation school bus plant closed in 2010 and moved to Tulsa, and a large facility announced by HP in 2008 for 1,200 jobs was later abandoned and is now leased by Gainwell. Westrock Coffee bought a 524,000 square foot facility in 2021, with 250 jobs expected.

An owner who has to relocate because of a layoff or a transfer is a common reason people look for a quick sale here. Stable anchors like the hospital and the university soften that risk, but they do not remove it.

sections.h2: How do colleges and schools affect selling a house in Conway?
sections.html:
Three colleges in town shape both the rental market and the pattern of home sales. The University of Central Arkansas has about 12,000 students, Hendrix College a little over 1,300, and Central Baptist College nearly 900.

Conway Public Schools serves most of the city, with about 10,000 students and 16 schools, which gives it the eighth-largest enrollment in Arkansas. Small parts of the city fall inside the Mayflower and Greenbrier districts, so check the district for a specific address before you describe the home to a buyer. Conway Christian School and St. Joseph Catholic School are the larger private options.

Landlords near campus often sell when a tenant turns over, because a vacant unit with deferred repairs is hard to show during the school year. A buyer who pays cash and takes the house as it is can fit that timeline better than a listing that waits for the next semester.

sections.h2: What does Conway's climate mean for the condition of a house?
sections.html:
Conway has a humid subtropical climate, with about 51 inches of rain a year and very little snow, around 2.3 inches. Roofs, gutters, crawlspaces and HVAC systems do most of the work here.

Temperatures have ranged from a record 115 degrees in July and August to a record low of minus 15. Average daily highs are near 72 degrees across the year, so a heat pump or air conditioner that is past its life is one of the first things a buyer inspector flags.

Severe storms are part of local history. An F4 tornado struck Conway on April 10, 1965, killing six people and injuring 200. Sellers with older roofs should keep any storm-damage paperwork, since buyers and lenders ask for it.

  • Check the roof age and any hail or wind claims before listing.
  • Look for moisture under the house after a wet spring.
  • Gather HVAC service records if you have them.

sections.h2: How and when are property taxes paid on a Conway house?
sections.html:
Faulkner County collects real estate tax between March 1 and October 15 each year, and anything paid after October 15 draws a 10% penalty. Real estate tax also accrues 10% annual interest after that date, according to the county collector.

The collector's main office is at 806 Faulkner St. in Conway, open 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays, with a second office in Greenbrier. You can pay online, by mail or in person. Personal property tax has to be paid before or with real estate tax, so an unpaid vehicle bill can block an online real estate payment.

An owner who lives in the home can apply once for the homestead credit, worth up to $600 a year, and must reapply after a move. At closing, the title company normally settles the current year's tax between buyer and seller, so ask for the tax figures early and confirm them with the collector. State law sets the payment window in Ark. Code 26-36-201.

sections.h2: What does a sale cost in Conway besides taxes?
sections.html:
Arkansas charges a real property transfer tax of $3.30 per $1,000 of the actual price on deeds that convey real estate. The state Department of Finance and Administration administers it, and the transfer stamp is bought at recording. Your contract states who pays it.

Other costs depend on the route you pick:

  • Listing with an agent: commission, repairs asked for after inspection, and carrying costs while the house is on the market.
  • Selling it yourself: marketing, legal paperwork and showings on your own time.
  • Cash offer: the buyer buys the house as it is, so there are no repair requests, and the closing timeline is set in the contract.

Recorded deeds in Faulkner County go through the circuit clerk, which also keeps a land records search online.

sections.h2: Who sells a house fast in Conway, and why?
sections.html:
Sellers in Conway usually have one of a few situations: an inherited house with no one to live in it, a rental with a tenant who left damage, a job move, or a mortgage that has fallen behind. Each one has a clock attached.

An inherited house needs the estate paperwork in order before anyone can sign a deed, and that process runs through the court. A house with a tax or lien problem needs payoff figures. A rental needs the tenant situation settled, since an occupied house limits what a buyer can do.

If any of these fits, the practical first step is to list the facts: who is on the title, what is owed, what condition the roof and systems are in, and when you need to close. A cash buyer can then base an offer on that list, and you can compare it with the net from a listing.

faqs.q: How long does a house take to sell in Conway?
faqs.a: It depends on the route. A cash sale can close as soon as title work is done, while a listing adds showings, buyer financing and appraisal time. The title company sets the actual date.

faqs.q: When are Faulkner County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Real estate tax is payable from March 1 through October 15. After October 15 the county adds a 10% penalty, plus 10% annual interest on real estate tax, per the county collector.

faqs.q: Is there a transfer tax when I sell in Conway?
faqs.a: Yes. Arkansas levies $3.30 per $1,000 of the actual consideration on deeds that convey real estate. Your contract says which party pays.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Conway house with a tenant in it?
faqs.a: Yes, but the buyer takes it subject to the situation. Tell any buyer about the lease and rent early, since it changes both price and timing.

faqs.q: Do I need to repair my Conway house before a cash sale?
faqs.a: No repairs are required to receive a cash offer, since the buyer prices the condition in. Compare the offer with what a repaired listing would net you after costs.
